title: Crestline Business Points Program Terms — Redemption
content:
These terms govern how the company points of a Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements agreement are redeemed.

### R1. Who asks and who benefits

Points belong to the company. They are redeemed only at the request of the travel manager or of a travel arranger on the roster, and only for a beneficiary who is on the active roster on the redemption date.

### R2. When points may be redeemed

Points are redeemed only while the agreement is active, or within the tier's post-termination redemption period, in calendar days, after termination. The agreement's status and its termination date are read from the agreement record.

| Agreement status on the redemption date | Redemption |
|---|---|
| active | may be made |
| terminated, redemption date within the post-termination redemption period after the termination date | may be made |
| terminated, redemption date after that period | not made |
| applied, under review, suspended or declined | not made |

### R3. What awards cost

- Award tickets cost the tier's listed award points for a domestic Crestline First round trip, a short-haul international Crestline Main Cabin round trip, a long-haul international Crestline Main Cabin round trip or a long-haul international Crestline Premium Economy round trip.
- The clause "Award tickets cost the tier's domestic Main Cabin round-trip award points" is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis for pricing a domestic Main Cabin round-trip award.
- Upgrades cost the tier's short-segment or long-segment upgrade points per segment, the segment being short or long by the segment-length threshold in miles of Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.

### R4. Summit status awards

On a tier where status awards are available, a roster traveler may receive Summit Silver for the tier's Summit Silver status-award points. The clause "Summit Gold for the tier's Summit Gold status-award points" is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis for pricing a Summit Gold status award. A status award lasts the tier's status-award validity, in calendar months, and never lowers a higher Summit tier the traveler already holds. Status awards in one agreement year may not exceed the tier's yearly status-award limit, counting the status-award redemptions dated from the latest anniversary of the approval date up to the day of the new award.

### R5. Paying for an award

The point balance must cover the whole award. Company points are never combined with a traveler's Summit miles, never converted to cash and never transferred to another agreement.

### R6. Award tickets as issued

Award tickets from company points follow the fare rules of Crestline Main Cabin, Crestline Premium Economy or Crestline First as issued, and they earn no points or miles.

### Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A request comes from a traveler on the roster who is neither the travel manager nor a travel arranger. It is not a request on which points are redeemed.
- A balance of 3000 points does not pay part of a 4200-point award; the whole award must be covered by the balance.
- On a tier with a yearly status-award limit of 2, an agreement that has redeemed 2 status awards since the latest anniversary of its approval date redeems no further status award in that agreement year.
